messages:
sasha: Heads-up — drafting a follow-up RFC for on-prem/air-gapped hotpatch rollforward + rollback windows. Short summary: allow a bounded reversible activation window (soft rollback) so operators can revert emergency patches without pulling full images.

maria: can you sketch operator UX? how does 'soft rollback' differ from full rollback? :thinking_face:

kevin: quick bullets: 1) activation delta includes a reference to previous activation hash; 2) reversible flag + TTL; 3) revert is a tiny delta that flips the activation pointer back; 4) all deltas are signed.

anne: is that going to blow up verifier-agent complexity? we already have activation sequencing, adding TTLs and reversible state could be tricky.

verifier-bot: note: verifier-agent today validates signed manifests and enforces activation ordering. it doesn't track rollback tokens or TTLs.

sasha: agreed — implementation idea to minimize state: use a short-lived reversible activation token stored as a single file with explicit semantics: write pending-activation -> flush -> swap symlink -> write activation-complete. reversible token contains previous-activation-hash + expiry timestamp. agent only needs to honor a single active reversible token per component.

maria: TTL control: operator-configurable per-cluster but with sane defaults (default 24h, max 72h unless enterprise policy). also UI should show countdown.

kevin: edge-case: powercut mid-activation. plan: make activation idempotent and durable: pseudo-steps in RFC:
```
1. write /var/lib/redwood/pending-activation.json (includes prev hash, token)
2. fsync
3. atomically update component symlink to new revision
4. fsync
5. write activation-complete marker + fsync
```
On restart, agent inspects pending vs complete markers and either completes or rolls back according to token state.
```

sre-oncall: emergency procedure: if rollback window expired but we need to revert, support an "emergency-unwind" bundle that requires root signing + multi-person approval logged in audit. this will be an explicit, non-automated playbook step.

anne: console UX idea: allow "pause rollback window" for a specific cluster when patching across maintenance windows. but require a justification note and audit entry.

maria: security: require KMS signing for normal deltas, HSM-backed key for emergency-unwind for Private deployments. also ensure replay protection using monotonic counters in manifests.

kevin: tests to add: simulate powerloss during activation, simulate replay attempts with old tokens, verify emergency-unwind can only be applied with appropriate signatures.

sasha: I'll update RFC: add sequence diagram, manifest header example, file-level atomicity checklist, and a short operator playbook for emergency unwind. also include sample console screenshots for pause/hold.

sasha: manifest sample to include in RFC:
```
{
  "bundle_type": "activation-reversible",
  "version": "1.0",
  "component": "runtime-agent",
  "new_revision": "rev-2026-03-01",
  "prev_hash": "sha256:abc123...",
  "reversible": true,
  "rollback_ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "signature": "kms:v1:..."
}
```

maria: looks good. please add the emergency-unwind signing policy details (who can sign, merkel-of-approvals) and we'll run it by security.

kevin: will stub tests and a small agent patch; keep verifier changes minimal — prefer to make the token ephemeral and agent-local.

deploy-bot: deploy-log: 3212345680 - RFC follow-up draft pushed to docs repo: https://stash.redwood.internal/docs/rfcs/offsite-hotpatch-rollforward-procedure.md
